newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Limited output lost after Rusplats strike.
newsitem.headline: Limited output lost after Rusplats strike.

text.p: Striking Rustenburg Platinum miners began the morning shift on Thursday after returning for the night shift on Wednesday and manager Anglo American Platinum Corp said only limited output had been lost in the stoppage.

The wildcat strike by 4,600 miners at the world's biggest platinum mine, Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd, which started on Monday night, had affected about 15 percent of the mine's total production, a spokesman said.
"Yes, the morning shift has turned up for work. Lost production is very limited. It's only 15 percent over less than three days," Amplats spokesman Johan Adler told Reuters.
He added that further details on how much platinum output had been lost would be available later.
Rustenburg produced 690,000 ounces of platinum in the six months to December 31, 1996, equivalent to around a quarter of world supply.
News of the strike fuelled a rally in platinum and palladium on Wednesday.
The problems at Rustenburg followed the suspension of members of the Mouthpiece Workers' Union and a company manager after an alleged attack on a member of the rival National Union of Mineworkers.
As a result, the workers did not turn up for Monday's night shift and a fight broke out at one of the hostels between strikers and employees who wanted to work, resulting in several injuries.
